Self-Care Checklist

Self-care isn't just bubble baths — it's the small, boring maintenance that keeps your mind and body running: sleep, movement, connection, and genuine downtime. This checklist is a menu, not a to-do list; pick a few each day rather than aiming for all of them. Use it as-is, or open it in Gisti to build your own, and see the rest of our health and fitness checklists.

Self-Care Checklist · 17 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Drink enough water through the day
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Get 7 to 9 hours of sleep

    A consistent bedtime and wake time matters as much as the hours.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Move your body for 20 to 30 minutes, even just a walk
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Eat at least one balanced, home-cooked meal
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Step outside for fresh air and daylight
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Take a real break from screens

    Even 20 minutes away from a screen resets your focus.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Do one thing purely because you enjoy it
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Connect with a friend or someone you love

    A short call or message counts — connection is a core need, not a luxury.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Write down 3 things you're grateful for
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Tidy one small space to clear your head
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Say no to one thing that drains you

    Protecting your energy is self-care, not selfishness.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Do a 5-minute breathing or meditation session
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Stretch or take a warm bath to release tension
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Set a limit on doomscrolling and social media
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Take any medications or supplements you need
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan something small to look forward to
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Check in with yourself: how am I actually feeling today?

    Naming an emotion takes the edge off it.

Frequently asked questions

What are examples of self-care? expand_more

Self-care spans the basics of physical health — sleep, hydration, movement, and decent food — plus mental and emotional upkeep like time outside, breaks from screens, connecting with people, and setting boundaries. It's less about pampering and more about the small habits that keep you resourced.

How do I build a self-care routine? expand_more

Don't try to do everything at once. Pick two or three items from a list like this that you can realistically do most days, anchor them to something you already do, and add more only once they stick. Treat the checklist as a menu you draw from, not a set of tasks you must complete.

What is the difference between daily and weekly self-care? expand_more

Daily self-care is the small, repeatable stuff — water, movement, sleep, a screen break, a moment of gratitude. Weekly self-care is the bigger recharge you plan for: a longer workout, time with friends, a hobby, meal prep, or a proper rest day. You need both.
